licenseOverrides.reason: Nuspec declares its licence only via the deprecated <licenseUrl> element (https://bitmiracle.github.io/libtiff.net/help/articles/license.html), not a machine-readable <license type="expression"|"file">, so the generator cannot resolve an SPDX id automatically. Verified BSD-3-Clause from the project's own license page, 2026-09-14.

bundledNotices.title: SkiaSharp native assets (libSkiaSharp) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: The nuspec declares MIT, which covers the SkiaSharp binding only. The native libSkiaSharp.dll this package ships is Skia compiled together with ANGLE, FreeType, libpng, libwebp, libjpeg-turbo, expat, ICU, zlib, HarfBuzz and others, each under its own licence; the package carries their combined notice file and it is reproduced here in full. -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true embeds that DLL into the shipped single-file executable, so every one of these obligations travels with the product. The identical file shipped by the Linux, macOS and WebAssembly variants of this package is attested as a byte-for-byte duplicate in noticesAlreadyCovered rather than reproduced four times.

bundledNotices.title: HarfBuzzSharp native assets (libHarfBuzzSharp) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: The nuspec declares MIT, which covers the HarfBuzzSharp binding only. The native libHarfBuzzSharp.dll this package ships is HarfBuzz built from the same Skia source tree as libSkiaSharp, and it carries the same combined notice file covering HarfBuzz, FreeType, ICU, Unicode data, zlib and the rest; it is reproduced here in full because the obligation attaches to this package's binary independently of SkiaSharp's. -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true embeds that DLL into the shipped single-file executable. The identical file shipped by the Linux, macOS and WebAssembly variants of this package is attested as a byte-for-byte duplicate in noticesAlreadyCovered.

bundledNotices.title: System.Composition (MEF 2) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: The System.Composition packages are pinned at 9.0.0 and ship the .NET 9 vintage of the runtime third-party notice, which is NOT the same document as the .NET 10 runtime-pack notice reproduced above: it carries the older 1991-2022 Unicode licence wording, 80 lines different. Reproduced separately for that reason. The five System.Composition.* satellites ship a byte-for-byte identical copy and are attested in noticesAlreadyCovered.

bundledNotices.title: Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: The nuspec declares MIT for the library itself. The package additionally carries a NOTICE file recording the third-party material Microsoft incorporated into it, under licences of their own; it is reproduced verbatim because nothing in the restore graph expresses it.

bundledNotices.title: ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime.dll) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: 6,121 lines covering the third-party code compiled INTO onnxruntime.dll: Intel Math Kernel Library, Eigen, protocolbuffers/protobuf, onnx, google/flatbuffers, google/re2, abseil-cpp, SafeInt, pytorch/cpuinfo and many more, each under its own licence. -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true embeds that DLL into the shipped single-file executable, so every one of those obligations travels with the product. This file was invisible to the generator's notice probe until 2026-09-14: the probe matched only the hyphenated spelling THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES*, and Microsoft spells it ThirdPartyNotices.txt. The identical file shipped by Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime.Managed is attested as a byte-for-byte duplicate in noticesAlreadyCovered.

bundledNotices.title: Microsoft.AI.DirectML (DirectML.dll) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: Separate from this package's LICENSE.txt reproduced above: 103 lines of attribution for third-party material compiled into DirectML.dll (Microsoft/GSL, Christian Rau's half float library, and Zstandard under the BSD licence). Self-contained single-file publishing embeds that DLL into the shipped executable. Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 widening of the notice probe to the unhyphenated ThirdPartyNotices.txt spelling.

bundledNotices.title: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: The nuspec declares MIT for the toolkit itself. The package additionally carries a 142-line notice for third-party material the .NET Community Toolkit incorporates under licences of their own; the source is compiled into the assembly this application ships. CommunityToolkit.HighPerformance carries a byte-for-byte identical copy and is attested in noticesAlreadyCovered. Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 widening of the notice probe.

bundledNotices.title: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis (Roslyn) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: Reproduced verbatim, INCLUDING its RTF container: Microsoft ships this notice as ThirdPartyNotices.rtf and the obligation attaches to the document as published, so it is copied byte for byte rather than converted, which would be an edit to a legal document. ONE deviation, and it is the only one: the file ends '}\r\n\0', and that trailing NUL - a Riched20 container terminator, not notice content - is stripped, because a single NUL makes git class the whole of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt as binary, so a pull request renders it as 'Binary file ... differs' and the human half of the freshness gate stops working on the one document where a silent change matters most. Nothing inside the document is touched. The readable content is the .NET Compiler Platform notice (MIT, (c) .NET Foundation and Contributors). The four other Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.* packages in the closure ship an identical copy and are attested in noticesAlreadyCovered. Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 widening of the notice probe.

bundledNotices.title: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: 260 lines, a different and longer document than the Roslyn ThirdPartyNotices.rtf above: it repeats the .NET Compiler Platform notice and additionally carries the Humanizer notice, so it is reproduced separately rather than attested as a duplicate. Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 widening of the notice probe.

bundledNotices.title: MSBuild (Microsoft.Build.Framework) - bundled third-party notices
bundledNotices.note: MSBuild's notice for third-party material it incorporates (LockCheck and others), shipped in a notices/ subdirectory under a spelling with no separators at all. Surfaced by the 2026-09-14 widening of the notice probe; the recursive search already looked in subdirectories, only the filename match was too narrow.

supplements.title: .NET 10 runtime and base class libraries
supplements.note: Embedded into the application by self-contained single-file publishing. They are part of the shipped artifact but never appear as package entries in the restore graph. The notice files shipped inside the runtime packs themselves are reproduced in section 3.

supplements.title: FFmpeg
supplements.note: FFmpeg reaches this application two separate ways, with different obligations. (1) The FFmpeg LIBRARIES ARE distributed: libavcodec and libswscale are compiled into VLC's libavcodec_plugin.dll and libswscale_plugin.dll, which ship in the release and declare themselves GPL version 2 or later. They are attributed in full under 'VLC plugins built under the GPL' in this section, together with the libraries statically linked into them. (2) The FFmpeg EXECUTABLES are not distributed: when no ffmpeg/ffprobe pair is found on the machine, FFMpegCore.Extensions.Downloader fetches a prebuilt binary from ffbinaries.com - a third-party mirror, not the FFmpeg project's own distribution - and the application runs it as a separate process. Those binaries are covered by their own licence, which travels with them; the Windows builds served by ffbinaries.com are GPL-configured (libx264 and friends), so GPL rather than LGPL-2.1-or-later is what the downloaded build is expected to carry. The earlier wording of this note denied bundling FFmpeg at all, which was false once the VLC plugins were audited.

supplements.title: Inter typeface (bundled by Avalonia.Fonts.Inter)
supplements.note: Copyright 2020 The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter). This Font Software is licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1. Section 1 lists Avalonia.Fonts.Inter as MIT (c) The AvaloniaUI Project, and that is correct for the Avalonia wrapper - but MIT is NOT the licence of the font data the wrapper carries. Avalonia.Fonts.Inter 11.3.13 embeds six Inter TTFs (Inter-Thin, Inter-Light, Inter-Regular, Inter-Medium, Inter-SemiBold, Inter-Bold, version 3.019) as Avalonia resources, and Program.cs calls .WithInterFont(), so those fonts ship inside the application and render its UI. The OFL requires this copyright notice, this licence statement and the full licence text below to accompany every copy of the Font Software. The copyright line, the licence statement and the version were read out of the fonts' own OpenType name table inside the shipped assembly (name IDs 0, 13 and 5); the licence text below is the canonical SIL text from https://openfontlicense.org/documents/OFL.txt, minus the per-font copyright template at its head, which this NOTE supplies for real.

supplements.title: VLC plugins built under the GPL (bundled by VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows)
supplements.note: Section 1 lists VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows as LGPL-2.1-or-later, and that is correct for libvlc and libvlccore themselves - but it is NOT the licence of every binary the package carries. The package ships 323 plugin modules for win-x64, and two of the ones this application depends on are built under the GPL rather than the LGPL: libavcodec_plugin.dll and libswscale_plugin.dll, which wrap FFmpeg libraries configured with --enable-gpl (the build stamp is present in both binaries). They are required, not incidental: removing them was tested and breaks HEVC and MPEG-4/AVI playback, because the remaining decoders fall back to Windows Media Foundation, which does not cover those formats here. Both plugins are statically linked (--enable-static --disable-shared), so code from several further libraries is compiled INTO libavcodec_plugin.dll rather than loaded from separate DLLs, and ships with it: LAME 3.100 (LGPL - build flag --enable-libmp3lame, with LAME's own version stamp, project URL http://lame.sf.net and runtime strings present in the binary), OpenJPEG (BSD-2-Clause, --enable-libopenjpeg) and libgsm (permissive, Technische Universitaet Berlin, --enable-libgsm). Their full licence texts are not reproduced here; they travel with the corresponding source named below, which is the route by which they are supplied. Note that LAME is LGPL and statically linked, so the relink provision of LGPL section 6 is satisfied through that source route rather than by replacing a file - unlike the LGPL libraries this application ships as separate assemblies. The other GPL modules in the package are NOT shipped - plugins/codec/libx26410b_plugin.dll (an H.264 encoder), plugins/lua/liblua_plugin.dll, plugins/audio_filter/libdolby_surround_decoder_plugin.dll and plugins/audio_filter/libheadphone_channel_mixer_plugin.dll are excluded in DiffusionNexus.UI.csproj, as is the whole lua/** tree (95 files of VLC web-interface assets, 16 of them GPL-2.0-or-later, which nothing can load once the Lua plugin is gone), as are the win-x86 and win-arm64 payloads in their entirety. The GPL set was determined from the binaries themselves rather than from package metadata, and DiffusionNexus.Tests/Licensing/VlcPluginLicenseTests.cs re-derives it on every test run so that a VLC version bump introducing a new GPL module fails the build instead of shipping unattributed. These plugins are separate files under libvlc/win-x64/plugins/, loaded at runtime by libvlc; they are not linked into the application executable, and this application is itself MIT-licensed, which is GPL-compatible. Corresponding source for the exact build is published by VideoLAN at https://download.videolan.org/pub/videolan/vlc/3.0.23/ - the binaries in this package identify themselves as VLC 3.0.23 'Vetinari', git revision 3.0.23-2-0-g79128878dd, read from libvlc.dll's version resource and libvlccore.dll's embedded version string rather than inferred from the NuGet package number. FFmpeg's own source is at https://ffmpeg.org/download.html. The full GPL version 2 text follows.
